{{short description|Symmetry with three or more colours}}
[[File:Threecolouranimation.gif|thumb|Three-colour symmetry operation of colour group ''p3''[3]<sub>1</sub>]]
'''Polychromatic symmetry''' is a colour symmetry which interchanges three or more colours in a symmetrical pattern. It is a natural extension of [[dichromatic symmetry]]. The coloured symmetry groups are derived by adding to the position coordinates (''x'' and ''y'' in two dimensions, ''x'','' y'' and ''z'' in three dimensions) an extra coordinate, ''k'', which takes three or more possible values (colours).<ref>Bradley, C.J. and Cracknell, A.P. (2010). ''The mathematical theory of symmetry in solids: representation theory for point groups and space groups'', Clarendon Press, Oxford, 677–681, {{ISBN|9780199582587}}</ref>

An example of an application of polychromatic symmetry is crystals of substances containing molecules or ions in triplet states, that is with an electronic spin of magnitude 1, should sometimes have structures in which the spins of these groups have projections of + 1, 0 and -1 onto local magnetic fields. If these three cases are present with equal frequency in an orderly array, then the [[magnetic space group]] of such a crystal should be three-coloured.<ref>Harker, D. (1981). ''The three-colored three-dimensional space groups'', Acta Crystallogr., '''A37''', 286-292, {{doi|10.1107/s0567739481000697}}</ref><ref>Mainzer, K. (1996). ''Symmetries of nature: a handbook for philosophy of nature and science'', de Gruyter, Berlin, 162-168, {{ISBN|9783110129908}}</ref>

== Example ==

The group ''[[Wallpaper group#Group p3|{{Tooltip|p3|p3}}]]'' has three different rotation centres of order three (120°), but no reflections or glide reflections.

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Uncoloured and 3-coloured ''p3'' patterns<ref name=Tilings>Grünbaum, B. and Shephard, G.C. (1987). ''[[Tilings and patterns]]'', W.H. Freeman, New York, {{ISBN|9780716711933}}</ref>{{rp|415}}
|-
! Uncoloured pattern ''p3'' !! 3-colour pattern ''p3''[3]<sub>1</sub> !! 3-colour pattern ''p3''[3]<sub>2</sub>
|-
| [[File:P3 pattern.svg|307px]] || [[File:Three-colour group p3(3)1.svg|307px]] || [[File:Three-colour group p3(3)2.svg|307px]]
|-
|}
There are two distinct ways of colouring the ''p3'' pattern with three colours: ''p3''[3]<sub>1</sub> and ''p3''[3]<sub>2</sub> where the figure in square brackets indicates the number of colours, and the subscript distinguishes between multiple cases of coloured patterns.<ref>Hann, M.A. and Thomas, B.G. (2007). ''Beyond black and white: a note concerning three-colour-counterchange patterns'', J. Textile Inst., '''98'''(6), 539-547, {{doi|10.1080/00405000701502446}}</ref>

Taking a single motif in the pattern ''p3''[3]<sub>1</sub> it has a [[symmetry operation]] 3', consisting of a rotation by 120° and a cyclical permutation of the three colours white, green and red as shown in the animation.

This pattern ''p3''[3]<sub>1</sub> has the same colour symmetry as M. C. Escher's [[M. C. Escher#Tessellation|''Hexagonal tessellation with animals: study of regular division of the plane with reptiles'']] (1939). Escher reused the design in his 1943 lithograph ''Reptiles'' and it was also used as the cover art of [[Mott the Hoople (album)|Mott the Hoople’s debut album]].

== Group theory ==

Initial research by Wittke and Garrido (1959)<ref>Wittke O. and Garrido J. (1959). ''[https://www.persee.fr/doc/bulmi_0037-9328_1959_num_82_7_5332 Symétrie des polyèdres polychromatiques]'', Bull. Soc. française de Minéral. et de Crist., '''82'''(7-9), 223-230; {{doi|10.3406/bulmi.1959.5332}}</ref> and by Niggli and Wondratschek (1960)<ref>Niggli, A. and Wondratschek, H. (1960). ''Eine Verallgemeinerung der Punktgruppen. I. Die einfachen Kryptosymmetrien'', Z. Krist., '''114'''(1-6), 215-231 {{doi|10.1524/zkri.1960.114.16.215}}</ref> identified the relation between the colour groups of an object and the [[subgroup]]s of the object's geometric [[symmetry group]]. In 1961 [[Bartel Leendert van der Waerden|van der Waerden]] and [[Johann Jakob Burckhardt|Burckhardt]]<ref name=Waerden>van der Waerden, B.L. and Burkhardt, J.J. (1961). ''Farbgruppen'', Z. Krist, '''115''', 231-234, {{doi|10.1524/zkri.1961.115.3-4.231}}</ref> built on the earlier work by showing that colour groups can be defined as follows: in a colour group of a pattern (or object) each of its geometric symmetry operations ''s'' is associated with a permutation ''σ'' of the ''k'' colours in such a way that all the pairs (''s'',''σ'') form a group. [[Marjorie Senechal|Senechal]] showed that the permutations are determined by the subgroups of the geometric symmetry group ''G'' of the uncoloured pattern.<ref name=atlas>Senechal, M. (1990). ''Geometrical crystallography'' in [https://archive.org/details/historicalatlaso0000unse_p0f2 ''Historical atlas of crystallography''] ed. Lima-de-Faria, J., Kluwer, Dordrecht, 52-53, {{ISBN|9780792306498}}</ref> When each symmetry operation in ''G'' is associated with a unique colour permutation the pattern is said to be perfectly coloured.<ref>Senechal, M. (1988). ''[https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0898122188902441/pdf Color symmetry]'', Comput. Math. Applic., '''16'''(5-8), 545-553, {{doi|10.1016/0898-1221(88)90244-1}}</ref><ref>Senechal, M. (1990). ''Crystalline symmetries: an informal mathematical introduction'', Adam Hilger, Bristol, 74-87, {{ISBN|9780750300414}}</ref>

The Waerden-Burckhardt theory defines a ''k''-colour group ''G''(''H'') as being determined by a subgroup ''H'' of index ''k'' in the symmetry group ''G''.<ref name=polyhedra>Senechal, M. (1983). ''[https://journals.iucr.org/a/issues/1983/04/00/a21969/a21969.pdf Color symmetry and colored polyhedra]'', Acta Crystallogr., '''A39''', 505-511,{{doi|10.1107/s0108767383000987}}</ref> If the subgroup ''H'' is a [[normal subgroup]] then the [[quotient group]] ''G''/''H'' permutes all the colours.<ref>[[H. S. M. Coxeter|Coxeter, H.S.M.]] (1987). ''A simple introduction to colored symmetry'', Int. J. Quantum Chemistry, '''31''', 455-461, {{doi|10.1002/qua.560310317}}</ref>

== History ==

* 1956 First papers on polychromatic, as opposed to dichromatic, symmetry groups are published by [[Nikolay Belov (geochemist)|Belov]] and his co-workers.<ref>Belov, N.V. and Tarkhova, T.N. (1956). ''[https://archive.org/details/crystallography-reports_january-february-1956_1_1/page/4/mode/2up Colour symmetry groups]'', [[Kristallografija|Sov. Phys. Cryst.]], '''1'''(1), 5-11</ref><ref>Belov, N.V. and Tarkhova, T.N. (1956). ''[https://archive.org/details/crystallography-reports_november-december-1956_1_6/page/486/mode/2up Colour symmetry groups]'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''1'''(6), 487-488</ref><ref>Belov, N.V. (1956). ''[https://archive.org/details/crystallography-reports_september-october-1956_1_5/page/482/mode/2up Moorish patterns of the Middle Ages and the symmetry groups]'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''1'''(5), 482-483</ref><ref>Belov, N.V. (1956). ''[https://archive.org/details/crystallography-reports_november-december-1956_1_6/page/n5/mode/2up Three-dimensional mosaics with colored symmetry]'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''1'''(6), 489-492</ref><ref>Belov, N.V. and Belova, E.N. (1956). ''[https://archive.org/details/crystallography-reports_january-february-1957_2_1/page/16/mode/2up Mosaics for the 46 plane (Shubnikov) groups of anti-symmetry and for the 15 (Fedorov) colour groups]'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''2'''(1), 16-18</ref><ref>Belov, N.V., Belova, E.N. and Tarkhova, T.N. (1959). ''More about the colour symmetry groups'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''3''', 625-626</ref> [[Boris Vainshtein|Vainshtein]] and [[Vladimir Alexandrovich Koptsik|Koptsik]] (1994) summarise the Russian work.<ref>Vainshtein, B.K. and Koptsik, V.A. (1994). ''Modern crystallography. Volume 1. Fundamentals of crystals: symmetry, and methods of structural crystallography'', Springer, Berlin, 158-179, {{ISBN|9783540565581}}</ref>
* 1957 [[Alan Lindsay Mackay|Mackay]] publishes the first review of the Russian work in English.<ref name="Mackay">Mackay, A.L. (1957). ''[https://scripts.iucr.org/cgi-bin/paper?S0365110X57001966 Extensions of space-group theory]'', Acta Crystallogr. '''10''', 543-548, {{doi|10.1107/s0365110x57001966}}</ref> Subsequent reviews were published by Koptsik (1968),<ref>Koptsik, V.A. (1968). ''A general sketch of the development of the theory of symmetry and its applications in physical crystallography over the last 50 years'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''12'''(5), 667-683</ref> [[Rolph Ludwig Edward Schwarzenberger|Schwarzenberger]] (1984),<ref>Schwarzenberger, R.L.E. (1984). ''Colour symmetry'', Bull. London Math. Soc., '''16''', 209-240, {{doi|10.1112/blms/16.3.209}}, {{doi|10.1112/blms/16.3.216}}, {{doi|10.1112/blms/16.3.229}}</ref> in [[Branko Grünbaum|Grünbaum]] and [[Geoffrey Colin Shephard|Shephard]]'s ''[[Tilings and patterns]]'' (1987),<ref name=Tilings /> by [[Marjorie Senechal|Senechal]] (1990)<ref name=atlas /> and by Thomas (2012).<ref>Thomas, B.G. (2012). ''Colour symmetry: the systematic coloration of patterns and tilings'' in ''Colour Design'', ed. Best, J., Woodhead Publishing, 381-432, {{ISBN|9780081016480}}</ref>
* Late 1950s [[M.C. Escher]]'s artworks based on dichromatic and polychromatic patterns popularise colour symmetry amongst scientists.<ref>MacGillavry, C.H. (1976). ''[[Symmetry aspects of M. C. Escher's periodic drawings]]'', International Union of Crystallography, Utrecht, {{ISBN|9789031301843}}</ref><ref>Schnattschneider, D. (2004). ''[[M. C. Escher: Visions of Symmetry]]'', Harry. N. Abrams, New York, {{ISBN|9780810943087}}</ref>
* 1961 Clear definition by [[Bartel Leendert van der Waerden|van der Waerden]] and [[Johann Jakob Burckhardt|Burckhardt]] of colour symmetry in terms of [[group theory]], regardless of the number of colours or dimensions involved.<ref name=Waerden />
* 1964 First publication of [[Alexei Vasilievich Shubnikov|Shubnikov]] and Belov's ''[[Colored Symmetry (book)|Colored Symmetry]]'' in English translation<ref name="Colored Symmetry">Shubnikov, A.V., Belov, N.V. et al. (1964). ''Colored symmetry'', ed. W.T. Holser, Pergamon, New York</ref>
* 1971 Derivation by [[Arthur Lee Loeb|Loeb]] in ''[[Color and Symmetry]]'' of 2D colour symmetry configurations using rotocenters.<ref name="Loeb">Loeb, A.L. (1971). ''[[Color and Symmetry]]'', Wiley, New York, {{ISBN|9780471543350}}</ref>
* 1974 Publication of ''[[Symmetry in Science and Art]]'' by Shubnikov and Koptsik with extensive coverage of polychromatic symmetry.<ref name=Shubnikov>Shubnikov, A.V. and Koptsik, V.A. (1974). ''Symmetry in science and art'', Plenum Press, New York, {{ISBN|9780306307591}} (original in Russian published by Nauka, Moscow, 1972)</ref>
* 1983 Senechal examines the problem of colouring polyhedra symmetrically using group theory.<ref name=polyhedra /><ref>Senechal, M. (1983). ''Coloring symmetrical objects symmetrically'', Math. Magazine, '''56'''(1), 3-16, {{doi|10.2307/2690259}}</ref> Cromwell later uses an algorithmic counting approach (1997).<ref>Cromwell, P.R. (1997). ''Polyhedra'', Cambridge University Press, 327-348, {{ISBN|9780521554329}}</ref>
* 1988 Washburn and Crowe apply colour symmetry analysis to cultural patterns and objects.<ref>Washburn, D.K. and Crowe, D.W. (1988). ''[[Symmetries of Culture: Theory and Practice of Plane Pattern Analysis]]'', Washington University Press, Seattle, {{ISBN|9780295970844}}</ref> Washburn and Crowe inspired further work, for example by Makovicky.<ref>Makovicky, E. (2016). ''Symmetry through the eyes of old masters'', de Gruyter, Berlin, 133-147, {{ISBN|9783110417050}}</ref>
* 1997 Lifshitz extends the theory of color symmetry from periodic to quasiperiodic crystals.<ref>Lifshitz, R. (1997). ''Theory of color symmetry for periodic and quasiperiodic crystals'', Rev. Mod. Phys., '''69'''(4), 1181–1218, {{doi|10.1103/RevModPhys.69.1181}}</ref>
* 2008 [[John Horton Conway|Conway]], Burgiel and [[Chaim Goodman-Strauss|Goodman-Strauss]] publish ''[[The Symmetries of Things]]'' which describes the colour-preserving symmetries of coloured objects using a new notation based on [[Orbifold]]s.<ref>Conway, J.H., Burgeil, H. and Goodman-Strauss, C. (2008). '' The symmetries of things'', A.K. Peters, Wellesley, MA,  {{ISBN|9781568812205}}</ref>
